task.name: WordNet two-hop hypernym plausibility
task.data: WordNet 3.1 glosses derived from the Round 025 corpus

features.svd_fit: unsupervised on all selected glosses, including held-out glosses

training.selection: best validation epoch; test evaluated once

shared_composition.operator_shape: two learned 48x48 ordered relation transforms with intermediate conditioning

measured_non_claims: This is two-hop link-plausibility classification, not autonomous language generation.
The SVD feature learner is transductive; this is not a strictly inductive benchmark.
Child synsets are disjoint, but candidate and middle synsets may recur across splits.
The native hyperedge strengths learn training records but held-out strengths remain exactly zero.
The native strength residual does not improve held-out AUC or cross-entropy in this experiment.
Hash collisions are possible in the 32,640-pair native address mapping.
The 256 NaN class labels and 32,385-cycle projection are not used as learned geometric features.
The native snapshot format is experimental, same-platform, and not crash-safe.
No competitive transformer, GNN, or retrieval baseline is included.
The inference score 0.8712 for the unfamiliar-definition example is a plausibility score, not a fact.

integration.host_language_math: experiment only; never on the production MTH path
integration.native_contract: future shared typed operators must be implemented in NaN16 and return UNAVAILABLE until native evidence exists
integration.next_gate: strictly inductive held-out definitions plus native operator composition inside the mirror layout
